operations.description: Emergency stop for outbound VoiceAgent dialing. Queued calls are cancelled and calls already in progress are ended within a few seconds, through the normal call-end path — billing, call records and analytics stay correct. **Inbound calls are unaffected**, as is the outbound traffic of every other company. The stop **expires on its own** after `duration_seconds`, so a forgotten stop cannot silence an account indefinitely. Sending the request again overwrites the window; sending `duration_seconds: 0` lifts it early. By default the stop covers all of the company's outbound calls. Supply `voice_agent_id` to stop a single VoiceAgent while the others keep dialing. Queued calls cancelled by a stop…

duration_seconds.description: How long to stop outbound dialing, in seconds. `0` cancels a stop that is currently active for the same scope. Maximum 86400 (24 hours).

voice_agent_id.description: Restrict the stop to a single VoiceAgent. Omit to stop all of the company's outbound calls. Must be a VoiceAgent belonging to your company.

Nothing is held, locked or recorded, so any of these contacts may be taken by an agent a moment later; treat the answer as a display hint, never a reservation. There is no partner-facing way to claim a contact. A campaign that exists but is not active, or whose queue is empty, answers 200 with an empty array — never 404. operations.description: Returns the company's surveys newest first, cursor-paginated. List items are summaries carrying a `question_count` instead of the questions themselves — fetch one survey by id for the full definition. Archived surveys are hidden unless `include_archived=true`.

query_params.name: limit

query_params.name: include_archived
query_params.description: Set to `true` to include archived items. Only the literal strings `true` and `false` are accepted — anything else is a 400.

operations.description: Creates a survey agents fill after a call. Omit `questions` to create an empty survey and add questions later with the replace-questions call. Question and option ids are server-generated — never send them. Attach the survey to a campaign via the campaign's `survey_id`.

name.description: Display name. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed before validation, so a blank or whitespace-only name is rejected with 400 (`name should not be empty` in `subErrors`).

questions.description: Initial question set. Omit to create an empty survey.

items.description: A question as sent in create/replace requests. Never carries ids — they are server-generated.

is_required.description: Whether the agent must answer. Defaults to `false`.

items.description: An option as sent in create/replace requests — no id.

operations.description: Returns one survey by id with its full ordered question set, archived or not. A survey belonging to another company reads as 404.

path_params.name: surveyId
path_params.description: Survey ID (BIGINT serialized as string in responses; send the numeric value).

operations.description: Updates the survey's `name` and/or `is_archived` flag — nothing else is patchable here; questions change only through the replace-questions call. Archiving (`is_archived: true`) is the survey's soft delete: there is deliberately no DELETE route, because archiving preserves the answers already collected — a `DELETE` on this path is an unmatched route and answers 404 `Route not found`. Restore with `is_archived: false`.

path_params.name: surveyId
path_params.description: Survey ID (BIGINT serialized as string in responses; send the numeric value).

body.description: Body of the patch-survey call. Only these two fields are patchable — questions change through the replace-questions call.

name.description: New display name. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed before validation, so a blank or whitespace-only name is rejected with 400 (`name should not be empty` in `subErrors`).

is_archived.description: `true` archives the survey (its soft delete), `false` restores it.

operations.description: Atomically replaces the survey's entire question set — this is a replace, not a merge. The body is the desired end state: existing questions (and their options) are deleted and the provided set is inserted in one transaction, ordered by `display_order`. `{"questions": []}` is valid and clears the survey. Question and option ids are server-generated — never send them; every replace mints new ids. Answers already collected are stored as immutable snapshots and are not rewritten by a replace.

path_params.name: surveyId
path_params.description: Survey ID (BIGINT serialized as string in responses; send the numeric value).

body.description: Body of the replace-questions call — the desired end state of the survey's question set. An empty array clears the survey.

items.description: A question as sent in create/replace requests. Never carries ids — they are server-generated.

is_required.description: Whether the agent must answer. Defaults to `false`.

items.description: An option as sent in create/replace requests — no id.

operations.description: Returns every event type an endpoint can subscribe to. Deprecated and internal types are not listed. Readable without a webhooks-enabled plan, so you can see what you would receive before enabling it.

query_params.name: include
query_params.description: `schema` adds the JSON Schema of the full webhook body for every version of each type.

operations.description: Returns one page of the company's webhook endpoints, newest first, including endpoints created in the Dashboard.

query_params.name: limit
query_params.description: Page size, 1-100. Out-of-range values are clamped and the effective value is echoed in `pagination.limit`.

query_params.name: cursor
query_params.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page's `pagination.next`. Pass it back unchanged. A cursor this API cannot use is rejected with `400 PAGINATION.INVALID_CURSOR`.

operations.description: Creates an endpoint and returns it with its signing secret. This response is the only time the secret is part of the resource; read it again with `GET /webhooks/endpoints/{endpointId}/secret`. The URL must be `https://` and point at a public host: private, loopback and other non-public addresses, internal names and non-ASCII hosts are rejected. A company can have at most 50 endpoints, Dashboard-created ones included. Send an `Idempotency-Key` to make retries safe. A retry with the same key and the same body returns the endpoint the first request created (201), even when the company has since reached the endpoint limit. The same key with a different body is rejected with 422. After the endpo…

url.description: `https://` URL on a public host whose name ends in a public top-level domain.

eventTypes.description: Event types to receive (see List webhook event types). Omit or send null for every event type. An empty list is rejected.

operations.description: Returns one endpoint. The signing secret is not included.

Changes any of `url`, `description`, `eventTypes` and `enabled`; fields you omit stay as they are. `eventTypes: null` subscribes the endpoint to every event type, including future ones. `url`, `description` and `enabled` cannot be null. `enabled: false` turns the endpoint off and its `status` becomes `disabled`; CloudTalk will not re-enable it automatically. `enabled: true` turns it back on, including an endpoint that was disabled automatically after repeated delivery failures (`status: failing`).

eventTypes.description: Replaces the subscription. `null` subscribes to every event type.

operations.description: Deletes the endpoint and stops delivery to it. This cannot be undone: the endpoint, its signing secret and its delivery history are gone.
Returns the endpoint's current signing secret, used to verify webhook signatures.
Replaces the signing secret and returns the new one. For the next 24 hours deliveries are signed with both the old and the new secret, so you can roll the new one out without dropping events.

Sends a sample payload of one event type to the endpoint. The payload has the real structure of that event with placeholder values. Delivery is asynchronous: use the returned `deliveryId` with the delivery endpoints; it appears there from the first delivery attempt, usually within seconds. The event type must be one the endpoint is subscribed to (an endpoint subscribed to every type accepts any), and the endpoint must be enabled. Test events and delivery retries share a limit of 10 per minute per company.
Returns one page of the events sent to the endpoint, newest first, without payloads. A delivery is listed from its first attempt. Payloads are kept for 30 days.

query_params.description: Page size, 1-100. Out-of-range values are clamped and the effective value is echoed in `pagination.limit`.

query_params.name: cursor
query_params.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page's `pagination.next`. Pass it back unchanged. A cursor this API cannot use is rejected with `400 PAGINATION.INVALID_CURSOR`.

query_params.name: status
query_params.description: Only deliveries with this final outcome. `failed` excludes deliveries that are still retrying.

query_params.name: eventType
query_params.description: Comma-separated event types to include.

query_params.name: since
query_params.description: Only deliveries created after this time (RFC 3339).

query_params.name: until
query_params.description: Only deliveries created before this time (RFC 3339). Must be later than `since`.

operations.description: Returns one delivery with the payload that was sent and every attempt on this endpoint, newest first, including the HTTP status your server answered and the first 4 KB of its response body. After 30 days the payload is no longer kept and `payload` is null.

path_params.name: deliveryId
path_params.description: Delivery id (`msg_...`). It is the same value as the `svix-id` header of the delivered request.

operations.description: Queues a new attempt of the delivery to this endpoint. Only a delivery this endpoint received can be retried on it. Test events and retries share a limit of 10 per minute per company.
